title: OpenFGA in Production
subtitle: Models API, writes, checks, and list-objects
content:
🔌 The Four Calls That Matter

  • Model write: publish a versioned DSL model (fga model write); keep every version — old tuples are interpreted by the current model.
  • Tuple write/delete: share-time and revoke-time facts (fga tuple write user:anne editor document:Q3).
  • Check: check(user:anne, viewer, document:Q3) → allow/deny at request time.
  • List-objects: which documents can anne view? — powers UIs and bulk pre-filtering without N checks.
OpenFGA lifecycle: store, model, tuples, check 
# Store -> model -> tuples -> check (OpenFGA CLI, pinned)
export STORE=$(fga store create --name pbac-lab | grep -o 'store_[A-Za-z0-9]*')
export MODEL_ID=$(fga model write --store-id $STORE --file model.fga | grep -o 'model_[A-Za-z0-9]*')
# --model-id is required once a store holds more than one model version;
# always pass it (copy-paste without it breaks after the second model write)
fga tuple write --store-id $STORE --model-id $MODEL_ID user:anne editor document:Q3
fga check --store-id $STORE --model-id $MODEL_ID user:anne viewer document:Q3
# -> {"allowed": true}   (editor => viewer, concentric)
# Store -> model -> tuples -> check (OpenFGA CLI, pinned) export STORE=$(fga store create --name pbac-lab | grep -o 'store_[A-Za-z0-9]*') export MODEL_ID=$(fga model write --store-id $STORE --file model.fga | grep -o 'model_[A-Za-z0-9]*') # --model-id is required once a store holds more than one model version; # always pass it (copy-paste without it breaks after the second model write) fga tuple write --store-id $STORE --model-id $MODEL_ID user:anne editor document:Q3 fga check --store-id $STORE --model-id $MODEL_ID user:anne viewer document:Q3 # -> {"allowed": true} (editor => viewer, concentric)

⏱️ Contextual Tuples (Verified Behavior)

Time windows and IP ranges ride along as contextual tuples supplied at check-time (docs pseudocode: ip-address-range:10.0.0.0/16, timeslot:18_19). Precision note: gating on them requires conditions with request context in the model — contextual tuples alone are just facts. Shape-illustrative condition (confirm condition syntax against your server version):

Condition + context: time/IP gating needs model conditions, not just tuples 
type document
  relations
    define viewer: [user with office_hours] or editor

condition office_hours(ip: string, now: string) {
  ip.startsWith("10.0.") and now >= "09:00" and now <= "17:00"
}
// check(user:anne, viewer, document:Q3,
//   context: { ip: "10.0.4.12", now: "10:15" },
//   contextual_tuples: [])  -> condition gates the direct grant
type document relations define viewer: [user with office_hours] or editor condition office_hours(ip: string, now: string) { ip.startsWith("10.0.") and now >= "09:00" and now <= "17:00" } // check(user:anne, viewer, document:Q3, // context: { ip: "10.0.4.12", now: "10:15" }, // contextual_tuples: []) -> condition gates the direct grant

And do not rely on the playground for this path: integration-test time/IP-gated checks against a real server.

🔍 Critical Review Notes

  • Revocation is tuple deletion — plus cache invalidation. A deleted tuple with a 60s check-cache is a 60s lingering grant. Size caches accordingly.
  • Write tuples transactionally with your domain writes: sharing-without-tuple (user sees nothing) and tuple-without-share (dangling grant) are both bugs — same transaction or outbox.
  • List-objects before check-storms: rendering all docs anne can view via per-doc checks is N+1 authorization; list-objects is the designed path. Bound it like any listing: type + relation filters, pagination, and product limits (see quiz q7 — unbounded reverse queries are a DoS vector).
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Trace how team-transitive paths resolve through two hops. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: A user unshares a document (tuple deleted) but keeps access for 60 seconds. Most likely cause?

options.text: Check-result cache outliving the revocation — invalidate on tuple writes
The model file was too large
Check API is eventually consistent by design for hours

questions.explanation: Revocation must invalidate cached allows. Cache TTL is a security parameter, not just a performance knob.

questions.question: A dashboard must show all documents anne can view. Efficient approach?

options.text: List-objects for (anne, viewer, document) — one designed call
Check every document id in a loop
Show all documents and 403 on click

questions.explanation: List-objects answers the reverse query (subject→objects) natively. Per-object checks for listing is N+1 authZ.

questions.question: Where must contextual tuples (time/IP) be tested?

options.text: Against a real OpenFGA server — time/IP gating needs conditions + context, not playground clicks

questions.explanation: Docs-verified limitation. Playground-green + server-red is the failure this question prevents.

questions.question: Sharing is saved to your DB but the tuple write fails. Result and fix?

options.text: User sees nothing (deny) — write tuples transactionally with domain writes
User gets admin — fail open is fine here

questions.explanation: Fail-closed saves you (deny), but the UX is broken. Same-transaction/outbox writes keep share-state and authZ-state consistent.

questions.question: Why keep every published model version?

options.text: Audits and rollbacks: know which semantics past decisions used

questions.explanation: Model edits reinterpret stored tuples. Version history lets you answer 'why was this allowed in March?' and roll back meaning.

questions.question: Sharing succeeds in the app DB but the tuple write times out. State?

options.text: Inconsistent — user sees nothing (deny) but believes it shared; reconcile via outbox/retry
Fine — the app DB is the source of truth

questions.explanation: Fail-closed saves the data but breaks the UX. Dual-write needs outbox reconciliation, not hope.

questions.question: List-objects returns 50,000 objects for a super-admin dashboard. Fix?

options.text: Paginate and scope the query (type and relation filters) — authorization output needs product limits too

questions.explanation: Reverse queries still need bounds. Unbounded authorization output is a DoS vector wearing a feature costume.

questions.question: You must rename a relation. Safe sequence?

options.text: Add the new relation, dual-write tuples, migrate checks, then remove the old — a schema migration
Rename in place on a Friday

questions.explanation: Relation renames reinterpret stored tuples. Expand-migrate-contract, exactly like database schemas.
